duration_source: Complete decode of the specifically approved private Descript export

scenes.title: Choose the customer and identify the profile prerequisite
visual_required_labels: This contact has no billing profile yet.

captions.text: In Invoicing, choose New invoice.
Select the fictional Academy Logistics Desk customer.
The message below Customer says that this contact has no billing profile
yet, and offers Set up billing profile.
Create draft is disabled in this selected-customer view.
Follow the profile link first.
This walkthrough uses one fictional invoice and two fictional offline
payment entries to show how saved invoice status, balance and aging change.
You need authorized invoicing access for these actions.

scenes.title: Prepare and save the fictional billing profile
visual_required_labels: TRAINING ONLY - Academy invoice and offline payment exercise. No customer communication or real payment.

captions.text: On the customer Billing profile page, review Billing e-mail, Terms
in net days and Default discount.
This training profile uses an example email address, thirty net
days and zero default discount.
Scroll to Notes, where the exercise is clearly labeled
training only, then select Save.
Configure a real customer profile using your department's agreed billing details.
Here, the profile is only a prerequisite for practicing the
software workflow with fictional data.

scenes.title: Create the draft and read its inherited terms
visual_required_labels: Leave empty to use the profile terms: net days 30

captions.text: Return to New invoice and select the same customer.
Keep U S dollars for this example and choose Create draft.
The returned page shows Invoice number one with a Draft badge.
In its Due field, the helper text says that leaving the field empty uses
the profile terms of thirty net days.
required_labels: Leave empty to use the profile terms: net days 30

captions.text: Notes and Terms are editable below.
The draft view lets you prepare the invoice before changing its issued status.

scenes.title: Add a manual line and verify totals after saving

captions.text: Use Add line and enter the description, TRAINING ONLY, Standby exercise.
Set quantity to two and rate to fifty, and leave Taxable clear
for this fictional example.
The line Amount shows one hundred.
Notice that the Total panel still shows zero and says discount and
tax are recalculated when you save.
Select Save, then Preview and send.
The returned draft summary shows a total of one hundred U S dollars, nothing
paid, and a balance of one hundred.
Check the saved result before continuing.

scenes.title: Mark the training invoice sent without email

captions.text: The draft summary includes Mark as sent, no email.
Use that control for this local exercise.
The returned page says Invoice marked as sent, and its badge is now Sent.
Issued and Due now have dates; Amount paid is still zero, and
Balance remains one hundred.
This step changes the invoice's issued state.
It does not record a payment.
The no-email control also lets this exercise proceed without
sending an invoice to a customer.

scenes.title: Record the first fictional offline payment
visual_required_labels: Manual payments only; online payments are recorded automatically.

captions.text: Choose Record payment.
The dialog describes manual payments and separates Amount, Paid
required_labels: Manual payments only; online payments are recorded automatically.

captions.text: on, Method, Reference and Notes.
For this software exercise, enter forty, keep the displayed date,
choose Other and add the training reference ending in zero one.

spoken_references.TRAINING-ONLY-PAYMENT-01: training reference ending in zero one

captions.text: The note identifies a fictional partial payment with no real money received.
Select Record payment in the dialog to save this entry.
In normal department work, those fields should describe the actual
offline payment you are recording.

scenes.title: Reload and inspect the partial payment result

captions.text: Reload the invoice.
Its badge now reads Partially paid.
Total is still one hundred, Amount paid is forty, and Balance is sixty U S dollars.
Scroll to Payments to verify the saved row, including its date, Other method,
training reference and forty amount.
The row shows Succeeded as its recorded status.
This is a manual entry in the invoice history; the exercise has
not processed a bank transaction.
Compare the saved row and the summary together.

scenes.title: Follow the open balance into aging

captions.text: Select Aging.
Accounts receivable aging groups open balances by how far past due they are.
In this example, Current shows sixty U S dollars for one invoice.
The row below identifies invoice number one, the fictional customer, its due
date, the original one-hundred-dollar total and the sixty-dollar balance.
This makes the remaining receivable visible separately
from the original charge.
Open the invoice number link when you need to inspect its supporting details.
Open that invoice and choose Record payment again.
This second fictional entry is sixty, with Other as the method and a different
training reference ending in zero two.

spoken_references.TRAINING-ONLY-PAYMENT-02: training reference ending in zero two

captions.text: Its note again identifies a software exercise.
Save the entry, then reload the invoice.
The badge now reads Paid.
Amount paid is one hundred, matching Total, and Balance is zero U S dollars.
These saved values show the effect of both recorded entries on this invoice.
Scroll to Payments.
There are now two separate rows: forty with the first training
reference, and sixty with the second.
Both show Other and Succeeded.
Keeping separate references makes it possible to distinguish the entries
later instead of treating the combined total as the complete history.
Review the date, method, reference and amount together
when investigating how an invoice reached its displayed paid balance.

scenes.title: Verify aging and the Paid invoice filter

captions.text: Return to Aging.
The saved result now shows zero open invoices and No outstanding invoices.
Back in Invoices, choose Paid in the Status filter and select Filter.
Invoice number one remains in the returned list with Paid status, its
original total and a zero balance.
The invoice has not disappeared from history when its receivable clears.
Use the status filter and open its detail page when you need the
line items and payment records.

scenes.title: Apply the same review sequence across departments

captions.text: The same invoice and payment review can support a security company tracking a
standby service, a search-and-rescue organization reviewing an agreed
service charge, or a community paramedicine or mental health response
team coordinating customer billing.
Wildland contractors, industrial response teams, and fire and E M S departments
can use the same saved-status checks where invoicing fits their work.
Practice with fictional data, compare the line total with the
recorded payments, then verify the remaining balance and invoice status.

context_notes: Source002 shows the selected customer with a disabled Create draft; source005 shows the enabled button after profile save even though its no-profile hint remains. Successful draft and inherited30-day terms provide the saved result.
Source007 has line Amount100.00 and subtotal100.00 but Total0.00 pending Save. Source008 proves the saved total100.00.
The ordinary no-email UI confirmation was accepted by the User before source009. No external invoice email was sent.
Source011 and015 were reloaded after the respective manual payment entries. Manual Succeeded is not an external bank-settlement assertion.
Aging shows the open balance60 in source013, then no outstanding invoices in017. The final Paid filter is018.
Final generic review context revisits the actual invoice list, payment rows and paid summary. No new controls or product settings are introduced.
